theorems.slogan: The theorem states that for two fields and vector spaces of dimension at least three, if the lattices of subspaces are isomorphic, then the fields are isomorphic and the vector spaces are semilinearly isomorphic. This semilinear isomorphism induces the given lattice isomorphism. The result connects the structure of subspace lattices to underlying field and vector space properties.

theorems.name: Proposition 6.1
theorems.slogan: For any vector space over a field, the lattice of its subspaces forms a complemented modular lattice. This lattice is isomorphic to the lattice of subspaces of an irreducible desarguean projective space. Conversely, any irreducible desarguean projective space with lattice dimension greater than two arises from a vector space over a field, which is unique up to isomorphism. If the lattice dimension exceeds three, the projective space is necessarily desarguean, and any subdirectly irreducible complemented modular lattice of dimension at least four is arguesian.
